name: Finance and insurance

bnote.641901: India's five largest private and public banks. Bank EBITDA is not a meaningful figure, so it is left blank.
bnote.642100: Holding companies. Bajaj Finserv, Bajaj Holdings and similar groups are left out because their operating companies are already counted.
bnote.651100: LIC and Max Financial are listed. SBI Life, HDFC Life and ICICI Prudential are left out because their parent banks are already counted.
bnote.651299: ICICI Lombard is left out because ICICI Bank is already counted.
bnote.661101: India's two listed exchanges, plus the three largest abroad.
bnote.661901: India's depositories and fund registrars, plus Visa.
bnote.663001: HDFC AMC and ICICI Prudential AMC are left out because their parent banks are already counted.

flags.mfsl: Max Financial's accounting profit is small compared with the value of its life-insurance business, so the P/E is not meaningful.
flags.paytm: Paytm has only recently turned profitable, so its P/E is very high.
flags.tatainvest: An investment company: profit is mostly dividends and gains, so it exceeds revenue.
flags.irfc: IRFC leases rolling stock to Indian Railways; nearly all revenue becomes profit, so margins look unusually high.

notes: EBITDA, EV/EBITDA and ROCE are not meaningful for banks and lenders, so they are left blank. Use ROE, net margin and P/E to compare them. Revenue for banks is total income as reported by the source.
